title: The evaluation-normalized transpose gives the costalk duality comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $D^b_{ctf}$ mean bounded constructible complexes whose derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

Let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure map. On the etale sites put $F=Ri_!=Ri_*$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], let $G=i^\times$ be its ambient right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and put $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$ for the structure-map right adjoint, $\omega_Z=G\omega_T$, and $D_W=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_W)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $\mu:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ be the exceptional counit. Assume $K,D_TK$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $i^*K,GD_TK$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, and $D_Z$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Assume the canonical projection formula [def-kun-projection-formula-map] $M\otimes_A^L FB\xrightarrow{\sim}F(i^*M\otimes_A^LB)$ for bounded constructible $B$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. Define $q_{M,N}:i^*M\otimes_A^LGN\to G(M\otimes_A^LN)$ as the exceptional-adjunction transpose of
$$F(i^*M\otimes_A^LGN)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}M\otimes_A^LFGN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu_N}M\otimes_A^LN.$$
Use evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_K:D_TK\otimes_A^LK\to\omega_T$ and tensor symmetry $\sigma$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. The tensor-Hom transpose $\alpha_K:GD_TK\to D_Zi^*K$ of
$$r_K=G(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}\circ\sigma_{GD_TK,i^*K}$$
is a natural isomorphism. More precisely, for every $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ the composite of tensor-Hom, exceptional-adjunction, and projection-formula bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,GD_TK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(FB\otimes_A^LK,\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(F(B\otimes_A^Li^*K),\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,D_Zi^*K)$$
is postcomposition with this particular $\alpha_K$.

proof.text: Use the canonical natural signed tensor symmetry derivedTensorSymmetry. It is the localization of the Koszul interchange, exactly the map characterized by the old etaleKoszulSymmetry witness. Opposite symmetries cancel by derivedTensorSymmetry_involutive. The definition boundarySigma now uses that real construction directly.

Use the already constructed ordinary-etale derivedTensorHomAdjunction₂ and the ambient exceptional adjunction. Their unary Hom equivalences, symmetry conjugations and the inverse canonical projection component give exactly the existing independent boundaryAlphaHomChain. No generic ringed-site global-sections or restriction comparison is needed.

For b:B→B′, invert the first-variable naturality square of the canonical projection map. Expand the seven Hom-chain factors. Apply naturality of the inverse symmetries, the tensor-Hom adjunctions and exceptional transposition. This proves theta_B(b followed by c)=b followed by theta_B′(c). The private abstract helper homChain_natural carries this calculation before specialization.

Evaluate the chain at identity of X=G RHom(K,W). Expand q, r, alpha and evaluation. Cancel the two opposite Z symmetries and the two opposite T symmetries, using the proved signed cancellation identity. Naturality of exceptional transposition moves the source symmetry and target evaluation through the adjunction. Uncurrying is tensoring with the exceptional counit followed by tensor-Hom evaluation, so the result is exactly alpha. This is homChain_identity and BoundaryData.alpha_eq_chain. Combined with the preceding step, theta_B(b)=b followed by alpha.

Let Y=RHom(LK,GW). The hypotheses make X and Y admissible. Put gamma=theta_Y inverse applied to identity_Y. The postcomposition identity gives gamma followed by alpha=identity_Y. Injectivity of theta_X then gives alpha followed by gamma=identity_X, by associativity. These two equations explicitly construct IsIso alpha.

For u:K→K′, invert the second-variable projection naturality square. Expand the Hom chain and use the parameter naturality of derivedTensorHomAdjunction₂ in each category and the ordinary adjunction naturality. This gives theta_B^K(b followed by G(Du))=theta_B^K′(b) followed by D_Z(Lu). Take B=G(DK′), b=identity and use the postcomposition identity and the identity-chain normalization. This proves exactly the displayed contravariant naturality equation.

theorem boundaryAlphaNormalization
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (n : ℕ) {Z T : Scheme.{u}} (aT : T ⟶ Spec (.of D.k))
    [IsSeparated aT] [LocallyOfFiniteType aT] [QuasiCompact aT]
    (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hPF : ∀ B : DerivedCategoryModule (boundaryCoefficient l E n) Z,
      DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible (boundaryCoefficient l E n) Z B →
      ∀ M : DerivedCategoryModule (boundaryCoefficient l E n) T,
      WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) T M →
      IsIso (boundaryProjection (boundaryCoefficient l E n) i B M))
    (K : DerivedCategoryModule (boundaryCoefficient l E n) T)
    (hK : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) T K)
    (_hDK : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) T
      ((boundaryDT (boundaryCoefficient l E n) aT).obj (op K)))
    (_hiK : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z
      (L(upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (boundaryCoefficient l E n)) i).obj K))
    (hGDK : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z
      ((boundaryG (boundaryCoefficient l E n) i).obj
        ((boundaryDT (boundaryCoefficient l E n) aT).obj (op K))))
    (_hdual : ∀ B : DerivedCategoryModule (boundaryCoefficient l E n) Z,
      WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z B →
      WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z
        ((boundaryDZ (boundaryCoefficient l E n) i aT).obj (op B))) :
    boundaryNormalizationConclusions (boundaryCoefficient l E n) i aT
      (WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) T)
      (WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z)
      (boundaryPFOnFiniteTor l E n i hPF) K hK hGDK
